function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning: The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. They likely want to run a command to start Docker service. On Windows, Docker Desktop runs as a service. But the command "docker start" is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker Desktop, you might use "Start-Service com.docker.service" or "dockerd". But the user says "start Docker on window using docker start." Maybe they want to start Docker Desktop via command line. We can use PowerShell: Start-Service -Name com.docker.service. Or use "docker start" to start a container. But they want to start Docker itself. So we need to provide a command to start Docker service. Use "cmd_controller_execute" to run a command. Provide a command like "powershell -Command \"Start-Service -Name com.docker.service\"" or "sc start com.docker.service". Let's use sc start com.docker.service. That will start the Docker service. So we call the function with command "sc start com.docker.service".
